question.text: Saraswati Capital AIF is valuing investee company Kavach Defence. Year-5 FCF is INR 120 crore; post-Year-5 perpetual growth 'g' = 4%; WACC = 12%. Using the Gordon Growth formula, what is the undiscounted Terminal Value at end of Year 5?

explanation.text: The Logic: TV = FCF(T+1) / (WACC - g) = [120 x (1 + 0.04)] / (0.12 - 0.04) = 124.8 / 0.08 = INR 1,560 crore. The Year-5 FCF must first be grown by (1 + g) to obtain the Year-6 cash flow before dividing by (WACC - g). The Trap: INR 1,500 crore = 120 / 0.08, which omits the (1 + g) growth on the Year-5 FCF. INR 1,000 crore uses WACC alone in the denominator and ignores perpetuity-with-growth. INR 1,250 crore arises from a denominator-side miscalculation. Note: The Gordon Growth model assumes growth 'g' is sustainable in perpetuity and strictly less than WACC; otherwise the formula does not converge.
